ai.literal: Decorum excellence because-it-gives, decorum even-than-life to-protect will-be.
ai.translation: Because decorum yields excellence, it must be guarded even more fiercely than life itself.
ai.modern: ஒழுக்கம் ஒருவனுக்குச் சிறப்பைத் தருவதால், அந்த ஒழுக்கத்தை உயிரை விட மேலானதாகக் கருதிப் பாதுகாக்க வேண்டும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme value of good conduct or decorum (ஒழுக்கம்). Because maintaining proper conduct brings true excellence and eminence (விழுப்பம்) to a person, it is the most valuable trait one can possess. Therefore, the text argues that decorum must be guarded (ஓம்பப்படும்) even more fiercely than one's own life (உயிரினும்). While life is naturally precious, the excellence born of good conduct makes it worth more than mere survival.

ai.literal: Having striven, having guarded, let one protect decorum; having examined, having guarded, even if researched, that indeed is the support.
ai.translation: Strive hard and guard your good conduct. Even if you examine and carefully research all other virtues, good conduct alone is your true support.
ai.modern: வருந்தியும் போற்றியும் நல்லொழுக்கத்தைக் காக்க வேண்டும்; பல அறங்களை ஆராய்ந்து போற்றித் தெளிந்தாலும், அந்த நல்லொழுக்கமே ஒருவனுக்குச் சிறந்த துணையாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme importance of good conduct or decorum ('ஒழுக்கம்'). The word 'பரிந்து' implies that one must protect their character even if it requires great effort or hardship. The second line states that even if one examines and practices many other virtues ('தெரிந்து ஓம்பி தேரினும்'), good conduct remains the ultimate and most reliable support ('அஃதே துணை') in life. The repetition of 'ஓம்பி' (having guarded) underscores the constant vigilance needed to maintain one's moral integrity.

ai.literal: Good conduct possession [is] noble birth; lapse [from it] degraded birth having become will end up.
ai.translation: Possessing good conduct is true noble birth. Lapsing from it will result in a degraded birth.
ai.modern: நல்லொழுக்கம் உடையவராக இருப்பதே உயர்ந்த குடிப்பிறப்பு ஆகும். அந்த ஒழுக்கத்திலிருந்து தவறுவது இழிவான பிறப்பாக முடிந்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: The couplet redefines what it means to be of noble birth. It states that true nobility comes solely from possessing good conduct. Conversely, any lapse from this proper conduct reduces a person's status. Such a failure will end up making them someone of degraded birth. Thus, character and behavior, rather than mere lineage, determine a person's true worth.

ai.literal: Even if forgotten, scripture acquiring is possible; a seer's birth, proper conduct diminishing, will be destroyed.
ai.translation: Even if a scholar forgets his scriptures, he can learn them again. But if his proper conduct diminishes, the nobility of his birth is destroyed.
ai.modern: கற்ற நூல்களை மறந்தாலும் மீண்டும் படித்துக் கொள்ள முடியும். ஆனால் ஒருவனுடைய நல்லொழுக்கம் குறைந்தால் அவனது குடிப்பிறப்பின் சிறப்பும் கெட்டழியும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the loss of learned knowledge with the loss of good conduct. The word 'ஓத்து' refers to chanted scriptures or learned texts, which can be relearned ('கொளலாகும்') even if forgotten ('மறப்பினும்'). However, 'ஒழுக்கம்' (proper conduct) is so fundamental that if it diminishes ('குன்ற'), the very status and nobility of a person's birth ('பிறப்பு') is permanently destroyed ('கெடும்'). The poem uses the figure of the 'பார்ப்பான்' (seer or scholar) to emphasize that even for those whose primary duty is learning, moral conduct is far more critical than intellectual retention.

ai.literal: Envy with the possessor wealth like, is not decorum with the one without greatness.
ai.translation: Just as wealth does not stay with an envious person, greatness does not exist for a person without decorum.
ai.modern: பொறாமை குணம் உடையவனிடம் செல்வம் நிலைக்காதது போல, நல்லொழுக்கம் இல்லாதவனிடம் உயர்வு இருக்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet draws a direct parallel between two negative traits and their inevitable consequences. The word aḻukkāṟu means envy, which prevents a person from accumulating true wealth or prosperity, the chosen meaning for ākkam here rather than mere creation. Similarly, oḻukkam refers to proper conduct or decorum, and its absence guarantees that a person cannot achieve greatness or high standing, the contextual meaning of uyarvu. By using the comparative word pōṉṟu, the text emphasizes that just as wealth shuns the envious, elevation in life shuns the undisciplined.

ai.literal: From good conduct they will not swerve, the strong-minded, from slipping harm happening having known.
ai.translation: Knowing the harm that comes from slipping into bad conduct, the strong-minded will not swerve from good conduct.
ai.modern: தீய ஒழுக்கத்தால் துன்பம் வரும் என்பதை அறிந்து, மன உறுதி உடையவர்கள் நல்ல ஒழுக்கத்திலிருந்து விலக மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: The couplet emphasizes that people with true mental strength will never deviate from proper conduct. The word 'உரவோர்' refers to those who possess 'உரம்', meaning firmness or strength of mind. Such individuals will not shrink or swerve ('ஒல்கார்') from good behavior because they fully understand the consequences. They know the inevitable harm ('ஏதம்') that occurs ('படுபாக்கு') from 'இழுக்கம்', which means slipping or falling into bad conduct. Thus, unwavering moral discipline is presented as the hallmark of a strong mind.

ai.literal: Through good conduct they will attain greatness; through lapse in conduct they will attain inescapable blame.
ai.translation: Through good conduct, people attain greatness. Through a lapse in conduct, they attain inescapable disgrace.
ai.modern: நல்லொழுக்கத்தால் மனிதர்கள் மேன்மையை அடைவார்கள். ஒழுக்கம் தவறுவதால் அவர்கள் நீங்காத பழியை அடைவார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the outcomes of maintaining and losing one's good conduct. The word 'ஒழுக்கம்' (good conduct) leads naturally to 'மேன்மை' (greatness or excellence). Conversely, 'இழுக்கம்' (a lapse or failure in conduct) results in 'எய்தாப் பழி', which means inescapable or unprecedented disgrace. The parallel structure emphasizes that just as surely as discipline brings honor, its absence guarantees lasting blame.

ai.literal: For goodness seed becomes good conduct; bad conduct always sorrow gives.
ai.translation: Good conduct is the seed that grows into all goodness, while bad conduct will always bring sorrow.
ai.modern: நல்லொழுக்கம் நன்மைகளுக்கு விதையாக அமையும்; தீயொழுக்கம் எப்போதும் துன்பத்தையே கொடுக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the outcomes of good and bad conduct. Good conduct acts as a seed that grows into lasting goodness and benefits. Conversely, bad conduct will inevitably and constantly yield sorrow. The metaphor of a seed emphasizes that decorum is the starting point from which all positive things in life grow.

ai.literal: Decorum to those who possess, are indeed impossible, evil things, even having slipped, with mouth speaking.
ai.translation: For those who possess good conduct, it is impossible to speak evil words, even by a slip of the tongue.
ai.modern: நல்லொழுக்கம் உடையவர்கள் தவறிக்கூடத் தங்கள் வாயால் தீய சொற்களைச் சொல்ல மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the deep-rooted nature of good conduct in a person. The word 'ஒழுக்கம்' (decorum or good conduct) is shown as a defining trait that prevents bad behavior. The phrase 'வழுக்கியும்' means 'even having slipped' or 'even by mistake', emphasizing that true decorum is an ingrained habit rather than just a conscious effort. Therefore, for those who possess such character, uttering evil words with their mouth is simply impossible ('ஒல்லாவே').

ai.literal: With the world to agree conducting oneself, many things even having learned, unlearned are they without wisdom.
ai.translation: Those who do not know how to conduct themselves in harmony with the world are truly unlearned, even if they have learned many things.
ai.modern: உலகத்தோடு ஒத்து வாழும் முறையை அறியாதவர்கள், பல நூல்களைக் கற்றிருந்தாலும் அறிவில்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: The word arivu can mean general knowledge or intellect, but here it specifically means the practical wisdom of proper conduct, fitting the chapter on decorum. This couplet defines true wisdom as the ability to live in harmony with the world. The phrase ulakattotu otta ozhukal emphasizes conducting oneself in agreement with the accepted norms of society. Even if a person has acquired vast textual knowledge, denoted by pala karrum, it is useless without this practical social wisdom. Therefore, the author concludes that such people are effectively unlearned.
